description: CapperTek review, checked 20 Nov 2026: how the pick marketplace works, who sets prices, refund terms, its leaderboards recounted, and user reports.
dek: A US pick marketplace and tracking site where any handicapper can list for free, set a price and post graded picks. CapperTek sells no picks of its own. Its records are more open than most tout pages and its own headline numbers check out, but "Verified" is a banner deal, not an audit, the leaderboards have no minimum sample, and its fees are non refundable.

status.label: Not verified
status.note: Watchdog has not audited CapperTek's grading or matched any CapperTek seller to a Watchdog graded record. We recounted its public leaderboards and two seller logs on 20 Nov 2026; this page reports what we could check and labels everything else.

short_answer: CapperTek is a real, long running platform. Its terms name Sports Media, LLC as the owner, its domain dates from Aug 2013, BBB has two files on it with no complaints, and its app is on the Apple App Store. It does not sell its own picks. It lists independent handicappers, tracks their picks and lets them sell access passes at prices they set.

Its pitch is transparency, and the numbers we could test held up. Its homepage said 104 handicappers were profitable over the last 30 days; we counted the 30 day leaderboard and found exactly 104 of 231. Pick ID numbers we saw had passed 3.5 million, consistent with its "over 3 million" claim. In two seller logs we downloaded, every pick was made before its game started.

The weak points are in what the labels mean. CapperTek's own FAQ says "Verified" means a seller put a CapperTek banner on its site so complaints can be routed, not that the record was audited. Picks can be voided. Leaderboards set no minimum sample, so the best ROI over 365 days belonged to sellers with one to nine picks. And CapperTek earns from the sellers it ranks through commissions, featured listings, banner ads and $450 sponsored posts.

Treat a CapperTek record as a useful starting point, not proof. Open the all time view, check the sample size, and remember that every seller listed is, in CapperTek's words, an individually owned and operated private entity.
pricing_intro: CapperTek does not publish one price list for buyers. Each seller sets its own access pass prices, which show on the seller's Purchase tab without signing in. The rows below are the platform rules as CapperTek states them on 20 Nov 2026, with two seller price lists as examples, and what CapperTek charges sellers.
pricing: Access passes to a seller's picks
Pass lengths of 1, 7, 14, 30 or 60 days (Sell Sports Picks page)
Seller offers extended access if a 14 day or longer pass finishes in the red
No guarantee shown on the pass page
Viewing records, leaderboards and free picks
CapperTek says pending picks stay hidden until 30 minutes after the start
Sales go directly to the seller
Check mailed monthly, $250 minimum payout, US sellers only (FAQ)
"a nominal monthly advertising fee", amount not published
Listing highlighted in green in the directory (FAQ)
guarantee: CapperTek itself guarantees nothing about results. The terms, last updated 8 Dec 2022 and re-read on 20 Nov 2026, say the site "makes no warranty as to the results that may be obtained from the use of the Website" and that "all fees and charges (including subscription fees) are non-refundable." The same terms say a Featured Handicapper subscription "can be canceled at anytime for any reason by the Provider without notice or refund."

Any guarantee comes from the individual seller. The BigAlsPicks profile, for example, says "Packages of 14 days or longer: if you finish in the red on our documented record for that window, we extend your access." That is more picks, not money back, and losses on the bets themselves are never covered.

Disputes with CapperTek go to confidential arbitration in the British Virgin Islands under its laws, according to the terms, even though the footer calls it "Proudly an American Company" and another clause points to United States law.

claims_note: How we checked: on 20 Nov 2026 we downloaded the full 30 day and 365 day leaderboards and counted every row, downloaded SportsCapPro's complete pick history (263 picks) and three days of BigAlsPicks history (22 picks), and compared pick times, totals and ID numbers with CapperTek's own statements.

The pages do not fully agree. The Buy page says picks cannot be deleted, while the FAQ explains that a pick "can ONLY be voided, meaning that there is still a record of it." The FAQ also admits that the default view hides older picks, which "might even make it seem like something fishy is going on." The Sell page promises "Zero fees or commissions," while the FAQ says CapperTek charges 30% when it takes payments for the seller. Each can be true in its own context, but a buyer should know voids and default windows exist.

The verification label is the biggest gap. The FAQ says Verified services "have been verified by us by placing a verification banner on their website," which means CapperTek "established an open line of communication directly with the owner ... so we can resolve any negative reviews or complaints." Pro Featured services are verified services that also pay a monthly advertising fee. Neither label says anything about whether the seller wins. The directory counted 2,458 Verified, 121 Pro Verified and 32 Pro Featured Verified services.

In a 2014 TheRX post, the CapperTek account described the company as a web development and marketing firm that works "together with many of the top name handicappers in the industry" on their IT and marketing, alongside running the directory. A tracker that also builds and markets for sellers has a reason to keep them happy.
record: CapperTek is a platform, so it has no single record. Each seller has a record kept by CapperTek, with picks revealed 30 minutes after the start. Here is what its own leaderboards showed on 20 Nov 2026, counted by us.
Last 30 days: 231 handicappers with picks, 104 (45%) up in units, median ROI -1.42%. Only 2 had 250 or more picks in the window, and both were down. 50 had fewer than 20 picks.

Last 365 days: 508 handicappers, 209 (41%) up in units, median ROI -1.6%. The longer the record, the better the odds a seller was up: of the 132 sellers with 500 or more picks, 77 were up, with a median ROI of +0.76%. That fits sellers who lose dropping out, as much as sellers who win staying. Sorted by ROI, the top five over 365 days had 9, 1, 1, 1 and 1 picks. The leaderboard sets no minimum, so sort by units and check the pick count.

We did not audit CapperTek's grading against game results. We found no outside review of whether voids, late posts or unit sizes are handled fairly. One check we could make held: our hand count of SportsCapPro's 263 picks matched CapperTek's totals to the cent of a unit (118-143-2, -93.01 units).

our_data.text: Watchdog grades picks captured from public posts before the game starts. In this edition no CapperTek seller is matched to a Watchdog graded record, so we make no claim about how CapperTek listed sellers perform.
our_data.context: For scale: of 132 CapperTek sellers with 500 or more picks over the last 365 days, the median ROI was +0.76%. On the Watchdog board, {{over60}} of {{established}} established accounts (100 or more graded picks) were at 60% or better, and the median established account won {{median_win}}% of its picks. At standard -110 odds a bettor needs about 52.4% to break even.

customers_intro: We found little independent talk from people who bought picks through CapperTek. Most mentions online are sellers advertising their CapperTek rank. We re-read the App Store, Sportsbook Review and TheRX threads, and both BBB files, on 20 Nov 2026. Below is everything we found and how much weight it can carry.

customers.text: Independent posts about CapperTek are few and span 2014 to 2026. Early forum talk was skeptical: in Nov 2014 a Sportsbook Review member who tried the site called it suspicious, and others replied that any rating service struggles to tell lucky sellers from good ones; in Aug 2015 another member alleged, without evidence, that CapperTek removed unfavorable reviews and favored services that paid it. Later evidence is milder. The App Store app rates 4.7 from 36 ratings, with one user praising its verified tracking and one complaining about pop ups pushing a monthly plan. Both BBB files show no complaints. On Reddit, nearly every mention from 2019 to 2026 is a seller promoting a CapperTek ranking, and one seller asked in 2026 whether those rankings mean anything. We found no buyer describing a lost payment or a refund dispute with CapperTek itself that we could open; the one purchase complaint we saw on the platform, about a seller, was withdrawn the next day.

A Sportsbook Review member said they had tried CapperTek, which rates handicapping services, and that it looked very suspicious, and asked if it could be trusted. Replies did not report a bad experience with the site; they argued that a rating service cannot separate lucky sellers from skilled ones, and one said any seller showing 60% over thousands of bets would be cooking the books.

A Sportsbook Review member warned others off CapperTek and another review site, alleging both deleted reviews that did not fit their business, removed negative reviews of services they endorsed, and paid members for reviews. The post gave no evidence, and later replies were general complaints about touts rather than about CapperTek.
An App Store reviewer praised the app for verified tracking of handicapper results and said it helps avoid scams and find handicappers to follow.
Another App Store reviewer complained about frequent pop ups pushing a monthly subscription, compared them to a pushy salesperson, and said he uninstalled the app.

A seller posted on r/sportsbetting asking whether CapperTek leaderboards are meaningful or just a vanity metric, after reaching fifth place overall. Only the title survives; the post body was removed.

Several Reddit posts from 2019 to 2026 are sellers citing their CapperTek rank or record as proof, for example a props seller claiming first place on the ROI leaderboard. These are sellers marketing themselves, not buyer reports.

The CapperTek account posted on TheRX describing itself as a web development, marketing and technology firm for handicapping sites that works with "many of the top name handicappers," and as the operator of the directory, where every service started at a "C+" rating. This is the company describing itself. One reply mocked how the directory rated another service.

BBB lists cappertek.com in Philadelphia, PA (A+, not accredited, business started 20 Oct 2014) and CapperTek in Scottsdale, AZ (not rated, started 1 Jan 2013), each with 0 complaints in the last three years and 0 customer reviews.

Our web searches found no CapperTek thread on Covers. A fresh Reddit archive search of r/sportsbetting on 20 Nov 2026 returned eight posts naming CapperTek, all from sellers or the 2026 question above; none was a buyer complaint about a CapperTek purchase. We did not read review sites that block automated reading.

conflicts: CapperTek earns money from the sellers it ranks: a 30% commission when it handles their payments, monthly fees for Pro Featured listings, $450 sponsored posts and banner advertising. A tracker paid by the people it tracks has a reason to keep them happy.

Its "Verified" badge means a seller placed a CapperTek banner and opened a channel for complaints, according to its FAQ; Pro Featured sellers also pay a monthly fee. Neither label is an audit of results.
In 2014 the company described itself as also building websites and marketing for handicappers. We do not know whether that work continues.
The terms say disputes go to arbitration in the British Virgin Islands under its law, while another section says United States law governs. The site publishes no street address.
strengths: Picks are revealed to the public 30 minutes after each game starts, so records are not limited to hand picked streaks, and every pick in the logs we checked was made before the start.
Its own headline numbers held up when we counted them: 104 profitable sellers out of 231, and a seller total that matched our hand count exactly.
Leaderboards show picks, record, average odds, units and ROI side by side, over windows from 3 days to all time.
Listing is free for sellers, so the directory is wide and not limited to paying advertisers.
A named operating company, written terms, and two BBB files with no complaints.
concerns: "Verified" is a banner and contact arrangement, not an audit of results, and Pro Featured sellers pay for their placement.
No outside audit of the grading. Picks can be voided, and profiles open on a short default window that can hide a poor long record.
The leaderboard has no minimum sample: the top five by 365 day ROI had between 1 and 9 picks.
Most sellers lose: 59% of sellers with picks over the last 365 days were down in units.
All fees and charges are non refundable under the terms, and disputes point to British Virgin Islands arbitration.
The platform earns from the sellers it tracks, and its customer reviews sit on the same site the sellers pay.
checklist: On any seller profile, switch the span filter to "ALL TIME" before you look at the record.
Look at the number of picks first, then units and ROI. Ignore any rank built on fewer than a few hundred picks.
Check how much of the record is parlays and how big the unit sizes are; CapperTek allows 0.1 to 11 units a pick.
Read "Verified" as "reachable", not "proven". Ask the seller how many picks were voided and why.
Read the seller's own guarantee and the CapperTek terms before you pay; CapperTek fees are non refundable.
Write down each pick yourself the moment you receive it, with the line you can actually get.
faq: It is a real platform run by Sports Media, LLC since 2013 that tracks and sells picks from independent handicappers, and the platform numbers we tested held up. We could not verify its grading against game results, because we found no outside audit, and its terms say fees are non refundable.

Viewing records and free picks costs nothing. Each seller sets its own price for 1, 7, 14, 30 or 60 day passes; on 20 Nov 2026 one featured seller charged $24.88 for a day and another $15. Sellers list for free and pay a 30% commission only if CapperTek handles their payments.

CapperTek keeps the records itself and reveals picks 30 minutes after each start, which is more open than most tout pages. Its "Verified" badge only means the seller placed a CapperTek banner and can be reached about complaints. Picks can be voided, and nobody independent audits the grading.
What does Pro Featured mean on CapperTek?

According to its FAQ, Pro Featured services are verified services that pay CapperTek a monthly advertising fee to be highlighted in green in the directory. It is a paid placement, not a performance award.
Can I trust the CapperTek leaderboard?

Use it with care. It sets no minimum number of picks, so sellers with one pick can top an ROI sort. Over the last 365 days 41% of sellers with picks were profitable; among those with 500 or more picks the median return was +0.76%.

As a free way to look up a seller's tracked history, it can help. Before paying any seller there, check the all time record and sample size; nothing on the platform refunds your fees or covers your betting losses.
